granary.voice: The wild grain grows for us now. We dream of a granary full of it, so that no winter can starve us.

great_bridge.voice: Our people work on the far bank and sleep there alone. We dream of a great bridge, so every night we can come home.

shelter_of_our_own.voice: The cave is cold and it is not ours. We dream of a roof we built, and a fire we can sit around together.

shrine_to_the_hand.voice: We have lived through a winter because of you. We want a place where we can thank the hand, and ask it things.

stone_circle.voice: We are many now. We want a circle of great stones, and a feast under it, so the sky knows we are here.

temple_of_the_hand.voice: We are a village now, with bread and bronze and cloth. By our fifth winter in this valley we will raise a temple where the shrine stands, big enough for all of us, with the hand on its doors.

entries.text: On the first night the hand lifted the fallen branch from the cave mouth, and we ran in out of the rain.
On the first day the hand lifted Ona for the first time. She did not fall.
On the first night the storm drove two of us to the cave: Ona and Tuk. The hand looked down and called us by our names.
On the second day we lit our first fire, and the hand watched over it.
On the second day the hand grew: Grip II. Lift 3 people; unlocks the scoop gesture. Granted free as the first gift.
On the fifth day we dreamed of something new: "A shelter of our own, and a ring of stones for our fire."
On the fifth day Oren walked into the valley and stayed with us. We were no longer alone.
On the fifth day the way to the valley floor opened, and we went to look.
On the fifth day Gor came to live with us.
On the fifth day Oda came to live with us.
On the sixth day we set stones in a ring around the fire, and sat together inside it.
On the seventh day we finished our first hut. That night we slept dry.
On the seventh day our dream came true: "A shelter of our own, and a ring of stones for our fire."
On the seventh day the hand grew: Strength I. Lift weight 4 (fallen logs).
On the seventh day the way to the western meadow opened, and we went to look.
On the seventh day Fen came to live with us.
On the seventh day Lema came to live with us.
On the seventh day Daro came to live with us.
On the seventh day Ama came to live with us.
On the eighth day we dreamed of something new: "A shrine to the hand, so we can speak to you."
On the ninth day we raised a shrine to the hand, and knelt there.
On the tenth day we built a store for our food.
We lived through our first winter. Nine of us saw the spring.
On the twelfth day our dream came true: "A shrine to the hand, so we can speak to you."
On the twelfth day the hand grew: Warmth. Hold over people or a fire to warm them.
On the twelfth day we finished the hunting lodge.
On the thirteenth day we dreamed of something new: "A circle of stones that points at the sky, where all of us can stand."
On the thirteenth day we built a rack to dry meat and berries.
On the sixteenth day Ulf was born to Lema and Oren, the first child of the valley.
On the seventeenth day the great stones stood in their circle at last.
On the eighteenth day the hand grew: Blessing. People you set down work 2x for 30 s.
On the eighteenth day Fia was born to Ona and Tuk.
On the eighteenth day Kai was born to Ama and Daro.
On the eighteenth day Mo was born to Oda and Gor.
On the twentieth day we finished the woodcutters' camp.
On the twenty-third day our dream came true: "A circle of stones that points at the sky, where all of us can stand."
On the twenty-fourth day Hana was born to Lema and Oren.
On the twenty-fourth day the Age of the Village began.
On the twenty-fourth day we dreamed of something new: "A granary, so we never go hungry in winter."
On the twenty-fourth day Celia came to live with us.
On the twenty-fourth day Hector came to live with us.
On the twenty-fourth day Freya was born to Ama and Daro.
On the twenty-fourth day Leif was born to Oda and Gor.
On the twenty-fourth day Corin was born to Celia and Hector.
On the twenty-sixth day the hand grew: Strong Arms. Carry a bridge timber (weight 6) and set it on a bridge plot.
On the twenty-sixth day we finished the the footbridge.
On the twenty-sixth day the way to the east bank opened, and we went to look.
On the twenty-sixth day Osric came to live with us.
On the twenty-sixth day Greta came to live with us.
On the twenty-sixth day Ivo came to live with us.
On the twenty-seventh day Aldo was born to Celia and Hector.
On the twenty-eighth day we finished the granary.
On the twenty-ninth day we finished the well.
On the twenty-ninth day we finished the cottage.
On the thirtieth day we finished the mill.
On the thirty-first day Rosa was born to Fia and Ulf.
On the thirty-first day Gor died of old age. We carved his name on the stones by the shrine.
On the thirty-second day Oda died of old age. We carved her name on the stones by the shrine.

On the thirty-fourth day Ama died of old age. We carved her name on the stones by the shrine.
On the thirty-fifth day we dreamed of something new: "A bridge over the Great River, so we can walk home at night."

memories.text: The hand brought us the log for our first fire.
The hand picked up our handprint stone, and its grip grew.
With the hand's help we made our dream come true: a shelter of our own, and a ring of stones for our fire
We lived through winter number 1.
With the hand's help we made our dream come true: a shrine to the hand, so we can speak to you
Our hunters went out from the lodge together and brought home a deer.
We learned to make stone tools. Now we gather faster, and we can fell trees.
The hand learned to bless us.
The hand blessed us and we danced at the fire all night. Our first festival.
Blessed by the hand, our hunters brought down the great elk.
We sewed clothes from the hides of the hunt, and the winter bit less.
We lived through winter number 2.
With the hand's help we made our dream come true: a circle of stones that points at the sky, where all of us can stand
We rebuilt our huts as cottages, with stone footings and room for a family
We painted the hand over our doors, so it knows our houses.
We stood on the bank of the Great River and looked across. Clay, and green stone in the rocks. We wanted the far bank.
The hand carried a great timber to the Great River for our bridge.
The hand carried a great timber to the Great River for our bridge.
The hand carried two great timbers to the shallows, and we raised a footbridge on them. We walked to the far bank and back.
We built a granary. The grain is safe from the damp and the mice.
We lived through winter number 3.
With the hand's help we made our dream come true: a granary, so we never go hungry in winter
Five of us pushed the raft into the Great River, and now we fish from boats.
We raised the great bridge. Now the far bank is a walk away, and everyone sleeps at home.
With the hand's help we made our dream come true: a bridge over the great river, so we can walk home at night
We lived through winter number 4.
We fired pots in the kiln. Now we can keep more of everything.
The fields gave and gave. We danced among the sheaves at the harvest festival, and thanked the hand.
The hand cleared the scree from the pass, and the road south to the river flats opened
The hand rolled the rockfall aside, and the hill quarry opened to us
We raised the Temple of the Hand where the old shrine stood, and painted the hand on its doors.
We lived through winter number 5.
Our first market day. Traders came down the valley, and some of them stayed.
With the hand's help we made our dream come true: a temple for the hand, with our hand painted on its doors
We lived through winter number 6.
